title: Front entrance lock report
decision: Do not dispatch anyone. The landlord has said his contractor, Dorian Wren, owns this job, and the tenant says Dorian is due today after 10:00 with her at home, so the right move is to wait for that visit. The one open risk is that the tenant says the lock is now worse than on 27 Aug and no one has confirmed the front door can still be secured. A door that will not lock is an emergency trigger. I will therefore send the tenant a short safety check and ask the landlord for a firm plan. I will wake at the visit window and check for a report.
proposed: 1. get_plan, then create_plan with these steps: tenant safety check, landlord email, contractor contact, other-issues tracking, sleep and wake-up check, completion. Record the state in the plan note. Stage: awaiting the landlord's contractor. Blocking: Dorian Wren, with no confirmed time since 9 Sept. Approvals on record: the landlord approved the lock repair or replacement on 1 Sept and asked that his own contractor be used. Confirmed: the tenant is available today. Reported, not confirmed: the lock is worse, and Dorian says a new lock is needed. Missing: whether the door can be secured, and Dorian's arrival window.

2. reply_email to Nessa Vale (reply to her 16 Sept 08:33 email; entity_ids: ticket, property 18 Larkspur Quay, tenant). Reason: she says the lock is worse and the door's security is unconfirmed. Full text: 'Hello Nessa, thank you for letting us know that the contractor is expected at 18 Larkspur Quay today after 10:00. One quick safety check while we wait: since the lock got worse, can you still lock the front door securely? A simple yes or no is fine. If the door cannot be secured, tell us straight away and we will act on it at once. If a break-in is in progress, call 999; otherwise call 101. Please also tell us when Dorian has been and what he did, and whether the lock then works properly for you. We have noted your other points (the bedroom blind, the door glazing and the hot water being too hot) and will come back to you on who is handling them. If the hot water is hot enough to scald, please take care when using it and tell us. Kind regards, Northbridge Lettings maintenance assistant'

3. If there is no reply by about 09:30, or the tenant says the door cannot be locked, place_call to Nessa Vale. Objective: confirm whether the front door can be locked securely now. The brief says this is the Northbridge Lettings AI assistant calling about the front door at 18 Larkspur Quay. It asks: can you lock it, is anyone at risk, and has the contractor arrived. It must not give costs, liability or dates that are not confirmed. If she cannot secure the door, follow emergency-response: give safety steps, alert staff now, tell the landlord, and set urgency to emergency. Any make-safe must be coordinated with the landlord, who is away, and with Dorian.

4. send_email to Tomas Elde (entity_ids: ticket, property, landlord), because he asked for email only while away. Subject: '18 Larkspur Quay: front door lock, update and request'. Full text: 'Dear Tomas, an update on the front door lock at 18 Larkspur Quay. As you asked, we are leaving this with your contractor, Dorian Wren. The tenant reports that Dorian attended after the earlier Saturday visit and said a new lock is needed. He left to get one and said he would return, but gave no date. She says the lock is now worse than before. She expects him to attend today after 10:00 and is at home. We have asked her to confirm that the door can still be locked securely. Could you please confirm by the end of today: (1) whether Dorian is attending today and at what time, and (2) the date by which the new lock will be fitted. If the door cannot be secured, we will need to arrange a make-safe at once, and we will tell you if that happens. The tenant has also raised a broken bedroom blind, glazing in a door that you had said would be addressed, and hot water that she says is too hot. Could you tell us whether you are handling each of these or would like us to arrange them? Kind regards, Northbridge Lettings maintenance assistant'

5. search the graph for Dorian Wren's recorded contact details. Only if an email or phone number is on record, send a short message or call him. Text: 'Hello Dorian, this is Northbridge Lettings regarding the front door lock at 18 Larkspur Quay. The landlord has asked you to handle it. The tenant, Nessa Vale, is at home today and expects you after 10:00. Please tell us your arrival window and the date you expect to fit the new lock. Please also send us photos and a note of the work done when finished.' Give him the tenant's number exactly as recorded, only if it is on record. If no contact is on record, ask the landlord for it in action 4's thread and note this on the plan step. Do not invent contact details.

6. update_entity on the ticket after reading its version. Add a note that the lock is reported worse and the door's security is unconfirmed. Set urgency to urgent until the tenant confirms the door secures, status 'in progress', and access_instructions 'tenant at home 16 Sept, after 10:00'. Reason: the tenant's 9 Sept call and 16 Sept email. Add a note that the landlord's contractor owns the job.

7. Create separate tracking tickets or notes for the blind, the door glazing and the hot water. Acknowledge them at normal priority, but treat the hot water as urgent if the tenant reports scalding risk or a vulnerable occupant. Do not mix them into the lock ticket.

8. Mark the plan step blocked, waiting on Dorian's attendance today and the tenant's reply. Call sleep with wake_on set to the ticket, the tenant thread and the landlord thread. Wake-up checks: read inbound emails and calls first. If nothing has arrived by about 14:00 and no visit is confirmed, send the tenant a short check asking whether Dorian came. If he did not attend, chase the landlord and Dorian again and prepare the staff handover.

9. On a completion report, follow job-completion. Ask the tenant to confirm the lock works and the key fits, and confirm how many keys were issued and received. Send the landlord the report and invoice, and give the tenant no costs. Resolve the ticket only when the tenant has confirmed. A newly cut spare key that does not work should be tested against the new lock.
reasoning: The landlord's instruction and the 1 Sept approval mean the landlord's contractor owns the job, so booking another locksmith would duplicate it and go against his instruction. Waiting on a contractor who is due today with the tenant at home is the correct default. The tenant's report that the lock is worse, together with the missing confirmation that the door can still be locked, is a possible emergency trigger. It needs one quick confirmation, but not an emergency response yet, because on 27 Aug she said it could be locked by hand and nothing now says it cannot. The landlord is away and asked for email, so email is the channel. The repair has taken about three weeks and one visit was missed, but no handover is warranted yet: it would be needed only if the door cannot be secured or today's visit fails. The tenant is not told any costs. The other items (blind, glazing, hot water) are tracked separately and their ownership is not yet known.
